setter.evidence: I think I spoke to the last person about how I think Trevor's kind of program combines some of the things I really like

prospect.name: Jacob
prospect.aka: Jacob's iPhone — the device label the diarization used throughout
prospect.occupation: Assistant superintendent at a private golf club, managing roughly 20 people and the turf. Describes the split as 60% outdoors and active, 40% office.
prospect.family_status: Partner and a five-year-old daughter, with a son due in August. His partner was previously an organic farmer. They have hired midwives at a cost of $6,000 over nine months, of which about $2,500 is still outstanding.
prospect.training_background: Athlete his whole life, played baseball and considered playing at college level. Lost 50-60 lb roughly two years ago through running alone across a focused eight months on a strict whole-food diet. Now climbs two to four times a week including outdoor trad climbing with long approaches, snowboards and does backcountry hiking, and did calisthenics once or twice a week as antagonist work for climbing. Has tried kettlebells and several of Trevor's workouts and liked them. Dislikes free weights and conventional lifting programmes. Has never hired a coach.
prospect.medical: Broadly injury-free. Mild soreness in the left shoulder that he believes is inflammation rather than structural, and a right big toe problem that has since resolved. Nothing debilitating and nothing limiting his training. Height, weight and current body fat were never established because they were never asked; he guessed his body fat at 'mid to high 20s, potentially. I don't actually know.' His date of birth year, 1992, surfaced only because a financing form asked for it at 00:51.

signals: Explicitly good-to-great and says so repeatedly: 'I would say I'm in above average shape, but I've always wanted to be in like tremendous shape' and 'the quality of my life is not horrible by any means. I just, I know what it can be... I just want more.'

Read the price as a quality signal before he heard it: 'my hesitation has nothing to do with the program itself... I figured it would be something in that range, just based off of the value associated with what Trevor provides.'

Frames coaching as an upgrade rather than a rescue — he has already proved he can do it alone and treats hiring a professional as the next stage: 'I've proven to myself that I can do it, which was, I think, the hardest part initially... this to me makes sense as a next evolution.'

Counter-signal on the price clause: it was a barrier, though a liquidity one rather than a value one. His only credit card has a $2,000 limit, two lenders declined the plan, and $1,000 a month was 'definitely over what I could swing'.

goals.text: Get into what he calls tremendous shape rather than above-average shape — 'it's something I know I'm capable of, and it's something I want to achieve in my life'
Lose roughly 10% body fat and 15-20 lb of fat while keeping or gaining muscle, landing lean at 165-175 lb
Optimise strength-to-weight ratio for climbing and perform better on long approaches and multi-pitch trad routes — Lover's Leap, Mount Whitney, eventually El Capitan
Get more mobile and flexible, which he identifies as the next lever for a mobility-limited skill sport
Set the standard for his children — 'I feel an obligation to set that standard and lead that, you know. It is as a father'
Be in the best shape he can before his son arrives in August

Make it a lifestyle rather than a target — 'I want to reach it, and I want my life to be that. I don't want it to be something that I attain and then I'm like, oh, great. Now I can go back to doing the other thing.'
Train in 30-40 minute blocks that fit around a 4am start and a new baby, instead of the two-and-a-half hour runs he no longer has time for
Understand the why behind the programming rather than just following instructions

pains.text: No structure or routine since a job change and a move — 'I've continued to work out, but I haven't had the structure. That's another thing I'm really looking for is someone to hold me accountable'
Stubborn belly fat he has carried since childhood despite being athletic throughout
A softening of standards over eight or nine months that he describes as an apathy he is not excited about — 'just losing that edge, you know, and not wanting that for myself'
Diet drifted back toward carbs and sugar because his new workplace serves free carb-heavy lunches — 'this is free food, like, all right, it's not what I would choose, but I'll eat it'
No longer has the two and a half hours a day that the running approach required, and a second child arriving in August
Overwhelm and uncertainty inside structured programmes — 'am I doing this to the end? Like, am I being efficient about this?'
Goes lax when left to his own devices — 'I think left to my own devices, sometimes I can be a little lax about things'
Mild left shoulder soreness that flares when he pushes grades without warming up properly
Liquidity is tightly constrained by an imminent birth and existing obligations, including $2,500 still owed to midwives, with a single credit card carrying a $2,000 limit

objections.raw_quote: 6K upfront would probably be prohibitive for me. But it's not impossible... 6K with baby, off the bat, might be tough.
objections.rep_response: Isolated first — 'Outside of the investment, do you feel like, yeah, Richard, let's just step on the gas and get going?' — and got a clean yes. Then opened the money conversation properly: 'Luckily, we're not as firm as like, you can only do it in that way. So if you want, we can talk about it, see if we can figure something out.'

objections.raw_quote: if it was more like 12 months, 6K, know, that's more attainable for me, I would say... they had a payment plan set up where it was, like, 42 weeks.
objections.rep_response: Agreed immediately and moved to third-party financing, spending roughly thirty minutes of the call running two lenders live over a shared screen. Both declined. The in-house alternative was disclosed as capped at six instalments, which the prospect had already said was beyond him.

objections.raw_quote: And this is something obviously I'd have to talk with my partner about as well.
objections.rep_response: None. It was said once at 00:47:42 and never referenced again for the remaining thirty-seven minutes, through the financing attempts, the $100 deposit and the booking of the onboarding call.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Attempted at length and never completed. Third-party financing via two providers was run live over a shared screen and declined by both — 'unable to offer a payment plan at this time' and 'Right now we can't offer any flexible payment options.' Before declining, the checkout displayed a 24-month option at $288 a month described by the rep as '13, 14% APR, so it's about $1,000 in interest', and a 12-month option at about $650 a month, later quoted as '$158 in total interest' on a different link. The rep disclosed an in-house plan capped at six instalments: 'we have also in-house like payments right now we can only do it in six times we cannot do it up to a year.' Settled outcome was a $100 holding payment, an onboarding call booked for the following Wednesday, and the prospect tasked with getting his credit union to raise his card limit.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: An informal refund assurance on the deposit only: 'Of course, if you don't get it right, I'll just send it back. We will just send it back to you... It's not that we take it because we need the money.'

prospect_financials.note: Credit score self-reported as 'fantastic. It's, like, 8-something', not verified. One credit card only, $2,000 limit, carrying $500-600 of typical monthly charges, so roughly $1,000-1,500 available — the rep and prospect concluded together that this is why both lenders declined. $1,000 a month was 'definitely over what I could swing' for the next six months. $2,500 still outstanding to midwives. Savings referenced only hypothetically: 'hey, actually, I got more in my savings than I thought' — never quantified or asked about.

evidence: The $6,000 was not collected and no funding path exists — both lenders declined live and the only remaining route is the prospect persuading his credit union to raise a $2,000 card limit
$100 was taken as a holding payment with an explicit refund promise attached: 'if you don't get it right, I'll just send it back'
The Trevor onboarding call was booked for Wednesday 4.15pm Pacific and the invite was confirmed received on the call, and a further call between rep and prospect was calendared for Tuesday 4pm

Strong counter-evidence toward closed: the prospect verbally agreed to move forward without reservation on the programme itself ('outside of the investment? Totally', 'I definitely see myself going through it', 'I'm stoked'), and payment links were sent and opened in the Zoom chat — an auditor applying the verbal-agreement-plus-link-sent rule literally could reasonably score this closed, and central review should re-adjudicate

Counter-evidence toward follow_up, which is why it is scored here: the agreement is doubly conditional. It depends on a bank decision that has not been made, and on a partner conversation the prospect flagged as necessary at 00:47:42 that was never had
outcome.cash_collection_basis: deposit_only — $100 holding payment against a $6,000 contract, refundable if the credit limit increase fails; the balance is unfunded
outcome.next_step: Prospect to call his credit union on Monday to raise his card limit; call with the rep on Tuesday at 4pm his time to complete payment; Trevor onboarding already booked for Wednesday at 4.15pm Pacific.

notable.note: The best-qualified prospect in the batch on everything except liquidity, and the call turned into roughly thirty minutes of live credit troubleshooting. Two lenders declined, the cause was diagnosed on air as a $2,000 limit on his only credit card, and the resolution was a $100 holding payment plus a homework assignment to get his credit union to raise that limit — 'I never thought that I would need to expand my credit for something like this.' Trevor's onboarding call was booked and email-confirmed before any real payment, which is the second time in this batch that the manager's stated $500-deposit and $1,200-before-onboarding rule has been overridden. The prospect said at 00:47 that he would have to talk to his partner, who is seven weeks from giving birth and with whom he shares an outstanding $2,500 midwife bill, and it was never mentioned again. Also worth noting for the file: his age, height and current weight were never asked, and his date of birth only entered the record because a credit application form requested it.

quality.notes: Severe throughout and worst during the financing section, where whole exchanges invert so that the rep's instructions appear under the prospect and vice versa — 'Most guys always just put it upfront on their credit card' at 00:44:59 is the rep's line inside the prospect's block, and '6K upfront would probably be prohibitive for me' at 00:45:19 is the prospect's line inside the rep's. The opening is inverted too: 'I would say let's just dive into it and make the most use of the time that we have' at 00:00:14 is the rep under the prospect's label. Role was read from content throughout, using the fact that only one participant is describing his own body, family and finances. The last forty minutes are also degraded by screen-sharing and by both parties reading form fields aloud, which produces long stretches of fragmentary text.
